source_text: Ὅρα μὴ εὑρεθῇς μακρο τέρας τῆς ζωῆς τὰς ὑποσχέσεις ποιούμενος. Οὐκ οἶδας τί τέξεται ἡ ἐπιοῦσα· μὴ ἐπαγγέλλου τὰ μὴ σά. Ἐπὶ ζωήν σε καλοῦμεν, ἄνθρωπε· τί ἀποφεύγεις τὴν κλῆσιν; Ἐπ' ἀγαθῶν μετουσίαν· τί ὑπερ βαίνεις τὴν δωρεάν; Βασιλεία οὐρανῶν ἤνοικται· ὁ καλῶν ἀψευδής· ἡ ὁδὸς ῥᾳδία, οὐ χρόνου, οὐ δαπά νης, οὐ πραγματείας χρεία· τί μέλλεις; τί ἀναδύῃ; τί φοβῇ τὸν ζυγὸν, ὥσπερ δάμαλίς τις ἀπειρόζυγος; Χρηστός ἐστιν, ἐλαφρός ἐστιν· οὐ τρίβει τὸν αὐ χένα, ἀλλὰ δοξάζει. Οὐ γὰρ δεσμεῖται ἡ ζεύγλη περὶ τὸν τράχηλον, αὐτεξούσιον ἐπιζητεῖ τὸν ὑφέλκοντα. Ὁρᾷς, ὅτι κατηγορεῖται Ἐφραῒμ, ὡς παροι-στρῶσα δάμαλις, ὅτι ἄτακτα περιπλανᾶται τὸν τοῦ νόμου ζυγὸν ἀτιμάζων; Ὑπόθες σου τὸν ἀδάμαστον αὐχένα· γενοῦ ὑποζύγιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἵνα μὴ, ἀφειμένος τῆς ζεύγλης, μηδὲ ἐλευθεριάζων τῷ βίῳ, εὐεπιχείρητος ᾖς τοῖς θηρίοις. Γεύσασθε καὶ ἴδετε, ὅτι χρηστὸς ὁ Κύριος. Γλυκύτητα μέλιτος πῶς ἀναγγείλω τοῖς ἀγνο οῦσι; Γεύσασθε καὶ ἴδετε. Αἴσθησις λόγου παν τὸς ἐναργεστέρα πρὸς πεῖραν. Ὁ Ἰουδαῖος τὴν περιτομὴν οὐχ ὑπερτίθεται διὰ τὴν ἀπειλὴν, ὅτι Πᾶσα ψυχὴ, ἥτις οὐ περιτμηθήσεται τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ ἐξολοθρευθήσεται ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτῆς· σὺ δὲ τὴν ἀχειροποίητον περιτομὴν ἀναβάλλῃ ἐν τῇ ἀπεκδύσει τῆς σαρκὸς, ἐν τῷ βαπτίσματι τελειουμέ νην, αὐτοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου ἀκούσας· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν μή τις γεννηθῇ δι' ὕδατος καὶ Πνεύμα τος, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ. Κἀκεῖ μὲν ὀδύνη καὶ ἕλκος· ἐνταῦθα δὲ δρόσος ψυ χῆς, καὶ ἕλκους καρδίας ἴαμα. Προσκυνεῖς τὸν ὑπὲρ σοῦ ἀποθανόντα; Οὐκοῦν κατάδεξαι αὐτῷ συνταφῆναι διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος. Ἐὰν μὴ σύμφυτος γένῃ τῷ ὁμοιώματι τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ, πῶς κοινωνὸς γενήσῃ τῆς ἀναστάσεως; Ὁ Ἰσραὴλ ἐκεῖνος εἰς τὸν Μωϋσῆν ἐβαπτίσθη ἐν τῇ νεφέλῃ καὶ ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, σοὶ τοὺς τύπους παραδιδοὺς, καὶ χαρακτηρίζων τὴν ἐπ' ἐσχάτων τῶν καιρῶν δειχθησομένην ἀλήθειαν· σὺ δὲ περιφεύγεις τὸ βάπτισμα, οὐκ ἐν θαλάσσῃ τυπού μενον, ἀλλ' ἐν ἀληθείᾳ τελειούμενον· οὐκ ἐν νεφέλῃ, ἀλλ' ἐν τῷ Πνεύματι· οὐκ εἰς Μωϋσῆν τὸν ὁμόδουλον, ἀλλ' εἰς Χριστὸν τὸν ποιήσαντα. Ὁ Ἰσραὴλ εἰ μὴ παρῆλθε τὴν θάλασσαν, οὐκ ἂν ἐχωρίσθη τοῦ Φαραώ· καὶ σὺ, ἐὰν μὴ παρέλθῃς διὰ τοῦ ὕδατος, οὐ χωρισθήσῃ τῆς πικρᾶς τυραννίδος τοῦ διαβόλου. Οὐκ ἂν ἔπιεν ἐκεῖνος ἐκ τῆς πνευματικῆς πέτρας, εἰ μὴ τυ πικῶς ἐβαπτίσθη· οὐδέ σοί τις δώσει τὴν ἀληθινὴν πόσιν, ἐὰν μὴ ἀληθινῶς βαπτισθῇς. Ἔφαγεν ἄρτον ἀγγέλων ἐκεῖνος μετὰ τὸ βάπτισμα· σὺ δὲ πῶς βρώσῃ τὸν ζῶντα ἄρτον, ἂν μὴ πρότερον ὑποδέξῃ τὸ βάπτισμα; Εἰσῆλθεν ἐκεῖνος εἰς τὴν γῆν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας διὰ τὸ βάπτισμα· σὺ δὲ πῶς ἐπανέλθῃς εἰς τὸν παράδεισον, μὴ σφραγισθεὶς τῷ βαπτίσματι; Ἢ οὐκ οἶδας, ὅτι φλογίνη ῥομφαία τέτακται φυλάσσειν τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ ξύλου ζωῆς, τοῖς μὲν ἀπίστοις φοβερὰ καὶ φλογίζουσα, τοῖς δὲ πεπιστευκόσιν εὐπρόσιτος καὶ ἵμερον ἐπιλάμπουσα; Καὶ στρέφεσθαι αὐτὴν ἐποίησεν ὁ Δεσπότης· ὅταν μὲν γὰρ ἴδῃ πιστὸν, τὰ νῶτα δίδωσιν· ὅταν δέ τινα τῶν ἀσφραγίστων, κατὰ στόμα προσαπαντᾷ.
thought_title: The Yoke of Christ and the True Baptism
orientation: Basil continues his direct address to the delaying hearer, urging immediate baptism by contrasting the easy yoke of Christ with the danger of remaining unbaptized.
pass_a_gloss: See that you are not found making promises longer than life. You do not know what the coming day will bring forth; do not promise what is not yours. We call you to life, O man; why do you flee the call? To a sharing of good things; why do you pass over the gift? The kingdom of heaven has been opened; the one who calls is not false; the way is easy, there is need of no time, no expense, no trouble; why do you delay? why do you shrink back? why do you fear the yoke, like some heifer unaccustomed to the yoke? It is kind, it is light; it does not rub the neck, but glorifies. For the yoke-strap is not bound around the neck, it seeks the one who draws it as free-willed. Do you see that Ephraim is accused, as a heifer driven to frenzy, because it wanders in disorder, dishonoring the yoke of the law? Put your untamed neck under it; become a beast of burden of Christ, so that, not released from the yoke, nor living without restraint in life, you may not be easy prey for wild beasts. Taste and see that the Lord is kind. How shall I announce the sweetness of honey to those who do not know it? Taste and see. Perception is clearer than every word for experience. The Jew does not postpone circumcision because of the threat, that Every soul which is not circumcised on the eighth day shall be destroyed from its people; but you put off the circumcision not made by hands, in the stripping off of the flesh, perfected in baptism, having heard the Lord himself: Amen amen I say to you, unless someone is born of water and Spirit, he will not enter the kingdom of God. And there is pain and a wound; but here is dew of the soul, and healing of the wound of the heart. Do you worship the one who died for you? Then accept to be buried with him through baptism. If you do not become united with the likeness of his death, how will you become a sharer of the resurrection? That Israel was baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea, handing down to you the types, and marking out the truth that was to be shown at the last of times; but you flee baptism, not one prefigured in the sea, but one perfected in truth; not in the cloud, but in the Spirit; not into Moses the fellow-servant, but into Christ the maker. If Israel had not passed through the sea, it would not have been separated from Pharaoh; and you, if you do not pass through the water, you will not be separated from the bitter tyranny of the devil. That one would not have drunk from the spiritual rock, if it had not been baptized in type; nor will anyone give you the true drink, if you are not truly baptized. That one ate bread of angels after the baptism; but how will you eat the living bread, if you do not first receive baptism? That one entered the land of promise through baptism; but how will you return to paradise, not having been sealed with baptism? Or do you not know that a flaming sword has been set to guard the way of the tree of life, fearful and flaming to the faithless, but to those who have believed accessible and shining with desire? And the Master made it turn; for when it sees a believer, it gives its back; but when it sees one of the unsealed, it meets him face to face.

choices.why: The compound means 'without experience of the yoke'; rendering it as a phrase preserves the image of an untrained heifer.
The verb means 'to live as a free man' or 'to act without discipline'; the phrase warns against being both yokeless and undisciplined, not against 'license' as a moral category.
The glossary does not cover this term, but the literal rendering preserves the Pauline contrast between physical and spiritual circumcision.

choices.english: in the stripping off of the flesh
choices.why: The noun ἀπέκδυσις means 'a putting off' or 'stripping off'; the literal rendering keeps the metaphor of removing the flesh.
rejected: in the removal of the flesh

choices.english: you may not be easy prey for wild beasts
choices.why: The adjective means 'easy to attack' or 'easy prey'; rendering it as a phrase preserves the vulnerability implied.
The idiom means 'turns its back' or 'retreats'; the literal rendering keeps the image of the sword turning away from the believer.

pass_b_english: Take care that you are not making promises that reach beyond your life. You do not know what the coming day will bring (Proverbs 27:1); do not promise what is not yours. We are calling you to life, my friend—why do you flee from the call? We are calling you to a share in good things—why do you pass over the gift? The kingdom of heaven stands open; the One who calls does not lie; the road is easy, with no need of time, expense, or trouble. Why do you delay? Why do you shrink back? Why do you fear the yoke like a heifer unaccustomed to the yoke? It is good, it is light; it does not chafe the neck but gives it glory. For the yoke-strap is not bound around the neck; it seeks the one who draws it of his own free will. Do you see how Ephraim is accused as a heifer driven to frenzy, because she wanders in disorder, dishonoring the yoke of the law? Put your untamed neck under it; become a beast of burden for Christ, so that, loosed from the yoke and living without restraint, you may not be easy prey for wild beasts. “Taste and see that the Lord is good” (Psalm 34:8). How can I announce the sweetness of honey to those who do not know it? Taste and see. Experience is clearer than any word for making a proof. The Jew does not postpone circumcision because of the threat: “Every soul that is not circumcised on the eighth day shall be cut off from its people” (Genesis 17:14). But you put off the circumcision not made by hands, which is brought to completion in baptism, in the stripping off of the flesh—even though you have heard the Lord Himself say, “Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God” (John 3:5). There, there is pain and a wound; here, there is dew for the soul and healing for the wound of the heart. Do you worship the One who died for you? Then accept being buried with Him through baptism. If you are not united with the likeness of His death, how will you share in His resurrection (Romans 6:5)? That Israel was baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea (1 Corinthians 10:2), handing down to you the types and marking out the truth that would be shown in the last times. But you altogether shun baptism—not one prefigured in the sea, but one brought to completion in truth; not in the cloud, but in the Spirit; not into Moses, your fellow servant, but into Christ, the Maker. If Israel had not passed through the sea, they would not have been separated from Pharaoh; and you, if you do not pass through the water, will not be separated from the bitter tyranny of the devil. They would not have drunk from the spiritual rock if they had not been baptized in type (1 Corinthians 10:4); and no one will give you the true drink unless you are truly baptized. They ate the bread of angels after baptism (Psalm 78:25); how will you eat the living bread unless you first receive baptism? They entered the land of promise through baptism; how will you return to paradise unless you are sealed with baptism? Or do you not know that a flaming sword has been set to guard the way to the tree of life (Genesis 3:24)—fearsome and blazing for the faithless, but for those who have believed, approachable and shining with lovely light? And the Master made it turn: when it sees a believer, it gives its back; but when it sees one of the unsealed, it meets him face to face.
notes: The source text contains several OCR-type spacing errors: 'μακρο τέρας' for μακροτέρας, 'ὑπερ βαίνεις' for ὑπερβαίνεις, 'δαπά νης' for δαπάνης, 'αὐ χένα' for αὐχένα, 'παροι-στρῶσα' for παροιστρῶσα, 'ἀγνο οῦσι' for ἀγνοοῦσι, 'παν τὸς' for παντός, 'τελειουμέ νην' for τελειουμένην, 'Πνεύμα τος' for Πνεύματος, 'ψυ χῆς' for ψυχῆς, 'τυπού μενον' for τυπούμενον, 'τυ πικῶς' for τυπικῶς. These have been read as single words in the gloss.

problems.why: The English "flee" loses the intensifying περι- prefix; "flee altogether" or "shun completely" captures the thorough avoidance Basil emphasizes, contrasting with Israel's participation.

problems.quote: released from the yoke and living without restraint in life
problems.source_quote: ἀφειμένος τῆς ζεύγλης, μηδὲ ἐλευθεριάζων τῷ βίῳ
problems.why: "living without restraint" mistranslates ἐλευθεριάζων—here it means "acting with license/insolence," not freedom. The warning is against being loose from the yoke AND living licentiously.
problems.fix: loosed from the yoke and living licentiously
problems.ruling: ἐλευθεριάζων τῷ βίῳ means living licentiously/dissolutely, not 'living without restraint' which is ambiguous.

edits.old: released from the yoke and living without restraint in life
edits.new: loosed from the yoke and living licentiously

fixed: περιφεύγεις has the intensifying περι- prefix, so 'altogether shun' better captures the thorough avoidance.
ἐλευθεριάζων here means acting with license or insolence, not freedom, so 'living licentiously' is correct.

problems.why: ἵμερον means 'lovely/desirable' (from ἵμερος, longing/desire), not 'gentle.' The sword shines attractively, invitingly for believers.
problems.ruling: ἵμερον means 'desire/longing'; 'gentle' misleads, losing the attractive, inviting sense.

fixed: Changed 'shining with gentle light' to 'shining with lovely light' because ἵμερον means 'lovely/desirable,' not 'gentle.'

problems.why: 'ἐλευθεριάζων' means living as a free man/unrestrained, not 'licentiously' with sexual connotation.
problems.fix: loosed from the yoke and living without restraint

edits.old: loosed from the yoke and living licentiously
edits.new: loosed from the yoke and living without restraint

fixed: Changed 'living licentiously' to 'living without restraint' because the source 'ἐλευθεριάζων' means living as a free man/unrestrained, not licentiously with sexual connotation.

dismissed.quote: even though you have heard the Lord Himself say
dismissed.why: Source says 'having heard the Lord Himself' — a participle of means/cause, not concession. 'Even though' adds concessive sense not in source.
dismissed.note: In this rebuke the participle carries a concessive force (you delay although you have heard the Lord), so 'even though' is a fair reading.

dismissed.quote: Experience is clearer than any word for making a proof
dismissed.why: πρὸς πεῖραν means 'for/toward experience/trial,' not 'for making a proof.' The Greek says 'sense-perception is clearer than any word for [gaining] experience.' The English 'making a proof' is wrong—πεῖρα is 'experience/trial,' not 'proof' in the sense of logical demonstration.
dismissed.note: Here πεῖρα means proof gained by trying something, which fits 'taste and see'; 'for making a proof' is fair, and the suggested fix is no better.
